text:
sam: FYI we
deployed the kernel selector bump last night and a subset of customers hit a dramatic drop in prefix cache reuse. Dumping quick figures.

sam: short summary (prod-eu, 24h):
```
overall_prefix_hit_rate  -> 52% (was 78%)
short_prefix (<40 toks) -> 38% (was 81%)
avg_kv_warmup_ms -> 72.1 (was 16.3)
```

sam: This looks tightly correlated with requests that include function/toolcall payloads. The hypothesis: we switched hot path hashing to use token ids instead of raw string, and the tokenizer mapping for the new kernel version changed ordering of some compound tokens. Same raw JSON -> different token ids -> different cache key.

anya: Do we have a tiny repro so infra or SDK folks can test? Is whitespace or system prompt changes also in play?

sam: Minimal repro posted to gist (copied here):
```
input: "Find user by id"
tool: {"params": {"user_id": 123, "verbose": false}, "op": "getUser"}
```
If params is {"verbose": false, "user_id": 123} we hit, reversed ordering misses.

jordan: That aligns w/ tokenizer shard remap. Also recall that in the kernel bump we changed tokenizer vendor shards; tokenization changed subtly for punctuation and JSON-ish strings. Hashing token ids will become non-deterministic across tokenizer versions unless we include tokenizer version in the key.

lee: Implementation detail: hot path currently chooses between hashing raw bytes and hashing token ids via a fast path. We flipped to ids for perf. The id hash avoids re-serializing but couples key to tokenizer mapping. Switching back to raw bytes is a small perf hit (~0.6ms median) but will restore correctness.

marta: Options:
- fallback: always compute both old-style raw-string key and new-style id key (dual lookup) -> doubles work on hit path
- tiered rollout: revert to raw-string immediately as an emergency; then implement stable canonicalization + append tokenizer_version to key format and rewarm

anya: I like the staged approach. Revert for immediate relief, then implement a long-term fix that prevents future silent collisions. Also we should normalize object key ordering for top-level tool params to avoid incidental misses when order isn't semantically meaningful.

jordan: Proposed permanent solution (sketch):
1) canonicalize toolcall objects by stable-sorting top-level object keys (leave arrays alone)
2) include model_name + tokenizer_version in cache key metadata
3) provide an opt-in parity-check mode: on miss, probe old key format in background and if found, copy to new key

sam: I ran a simulation: adding tokenizer_version to the key recovered ~12 pct points; stable-sorting top-level keys recovered ~24 points; combined exceeds baseline in our cohort. Simulation attached.

lee: Concern: adding tokenizer_version changes the key namespace so existing keys become stale. If we flip format we need a rewarm plan or dual-lookup. Dual-lookup adds latency and complexity.

marta: Rewarm plan suggestion: select top-50 affected customers + top 200 routes; replay their last 72h of requests into a rewarm job that computes new keys and writes them. Also enable a shadow path that computes new keys in parallel for telemetry before full switch.

anya: We should also instrument/emit metrics for token_version and key-format so console + alerts can surface tokenizer drift events.

sam: My recommended rollout sequence:
A) hotfix: revert to raw-string hashing on hot path (low risk rollback) -> immediate hit-rate recovery
B) implement canonicalizer + key versioning behind feature flag (dev/testing)
C) run rewarm pipeline + shadow mode for a week
D) flip flag for canary -> monitor -> prod

jordan: I'll open an RFC with canonicalization rules and examples. Will include unit fuzz tests for permutations of JSON object orders and tokenizer shards.

lee: I'll cut the hotfix canary PR today (single-line switch back to raw hashing). CI/DEPLOY: canary pool only. If health looks good we'll promote.

marta: I'll draft replay job and cost estimate. Early ballpark: rehydrating 72h for top-50 will be cheap CPU IO (no GPUs unless we simulate full kernel exec) but if we need tokenization parity runs we might need a small GPU fleet for 6-8 hours.

deploy-bot: sam requested raw-string-hash revert in canary. CI queued.

anya: Tests: add a regression test fixture that fuzzes JSON arg key order, varied whitespace, and toggles tokenizer shards to ensure both old and new keying are covered. Gate the RFC by passing that suite.

sam: I'll track PRs and add a small dashboard showing hit-rate by tokenizer_version per-customer.

lee: PR posted -> link in the follow-up thread. Cutting canary now.

jordan: RFC stub: will add examples of tool args where ordering matters (arrays) vs not (objects) and propose docs for SDKs to encourage deterministic param ordering for customers who care.

marta: Once we have shadow telemetry we can measure rewarm efficiency and estimate how long to keep both formats active.

sam: Thanks team. Prioritize hotfix canary and the telemetry panel—those will buy us time. Will close this thread after canary looks healthy and open follow-ups for RFC and rewarm job.
